Corollary
[Thin-part components in dimension three] 1. Corollary 5.10.2\group thick-thin geometrySource: thurston:page-0127 For sufficiently small $\eps $, every component of the thin part of a complete oriented hyperbolic $3$--manifold is either a horoball modulo $\Z $ or $\Z \oplus \Z $, or a tubular neighborhood $B_r(g)$ of a geodesic modulo $\Z $; $r=0$ is allowed.
Proof

\sketch Small-displacement parabolics generate concentric horoballs, while hyperbolics generate concentric solid cylinders. Overlap forces commutation by the preceding theorem, so each component has one of these two forms.
